top.title: DEP-Agent: electrode patterns and frequency schedules for a label-free circulating tumour cell (CTC) chip (merges seed S1 with the DEP-Agent idea)
top.description: ApoStream is a commercial chip that separates cancer cells from blood by dielectrophoresis: electrodes on the chip floor create electric-field gradients that pull cells down or let them float, depending on each cell's electrical properties. An AI agent writes code that produces an electrode pattern (finger width and gap, segments driven at different frequencies, angled steering sections), a chamber height and a schedule for voltage, frequency and flow. Each design is scored by an analytic Fourier-series field above the electrodes plus particle tracing of about 10^5 virtual cells drawn from measured cancer-line and blood-cell properties, run on the GPU over many designs at once. The agent reads which cell lines leak and why, then writes the next batch. The output is a printable electrode mask. Corrections: monocytes (crossover 95-113 kHz) are the hard contaminant, not T or B cells (149-221 kHz). The NCI-60 range is 11.6-36.3 mF/m2 and 23.4-102 kHz once the leukaemia lines are included. ApoStream's results paper tested 45-65 kHz. Throughput is set by how many PBMCs load onto the chamber floor (about 12 million cells per 7.5 mL draw), which a single-cell model does not represent, so throughput claims must be stated as model-limited.
top.scores: hardware 5, AI loop 4, biotech/money 4, visual 5, parallelism 4, feasibility 4, honesty 4 = 30/35
top.verified: Opened PMC3396706: SKOV3 75.4% and MDA-MB-231 71.2% recovery, about 60 min per 7.5 mL, 18-25 uL/min collection, 50 um spacing, 2-4.5 Vpp, 30 mS/m, cancer crossover 30-40 kHz vs PBMC 90-140 kHz, about 30 um levitation, 2 to 4 Vpp cuts PBMC contamination without changing cancer capture, 99.85% (45 kHz) and 99.33% (65 kHz) PBMC depletion. Opened PMC3754903 (Gascoyne 2013): membrane capacitance, crossover and radius per NCI-60 line and per blood cell type; cytoplasm conductivity is NOT given (needs another source, unverified). Morgan et al. 2001 Fourier-series DEP field solution exists (eprints.soton.ac.uk/258927, found by search, not opened). ApoStream is sold as a lab service by Precision for Medicine (precisionformedicine.com, search result). Prior art found: COMSOL electrode-shape sweeps (Sci Rep 2022, Microfluid Nanofluid 2023) and response-surface optimisation of 3 parameters (AIP 2026 news item). No ML or agent search over DEP electrode geometry was found. An LLM agent writing chip CAD exists for microwells (arXiv 2510.13883, opened), so 'agent writes chip code' alone is not novel.
top.main_risk: The hydrodynamic lift term is empirical and must be calibrated to the 30 um levitation height, and cell crowding on the floor, adhesion and 3-D edge effects are not modelled. Absolute recovery may miss even when the trends match, so claim gains relative to the simulated ApoStream baseline. Prior art is close in method (simulated electrode sweeps), so the novelty must come from the agent writing multi-frequency topologies plus population-scale GPU scoring.
top.headline_metric: Cells processed per hour (in units of 7.5 mL blood-draw equivalents) at at least 70% predicted recovery across the NCI-60 solid-tumour panel and at least 99.33% PBMC depletion, against the simulated ApoStream operating point (50 um, 45-65 kHz, 1 draw per hour). Second number: designs times cells evaluated per second on GPU versus a NumPy CPU loop, measured on the day.

top.title: ReadUntil Agent: agent-written adaptive-sampling policies for a nanopore sequencing chip, targeting faster resistance-gene calls
top.description: A MinION flow cell is a CMOS sensor chip with 512 nanopore channels. Through the ReadUntil interface, software can eject a DNA molecule after reading its first few hundred bases. An agent writes keep-or-eject policies as JAX functions: how long to read before deciding, when to switch from depleting human DNA to enriching resistance genes once the species is called, and per-channel strategy splits. Each policy is scored on thousands of simulated flow cells at once. Correction: the clinical bottleneck is the resistance (AMR) call, not species ID. In the 2024 positive-blood-culture study, species could be identified from the first hour of reads but full AMR prediction took a 15-hour run. Frame the problem as positive blood cultures and respiratory samples, not raw blood. Charalampous 2019 was lower respiratory infection, with 96.6% sensitivity but 41.7% specificity before confirmatory PCR. Sponsor hook: decision latency D is an explicit model parameter, so the demo can show how much faster an inference chip would make the diagnosis.
top.scores: hardware 4, AI loop 5, biotech/money 5, visual 3, parallelism 5, feasibility 5, honesty 3 = 30/35
top.verified: Opened PMC8785595 (Martin 2022): closed-form enrichment e = (R+CS)/(x(R+CS)+(1-x)(DS+CS)), which is algebraically the same as the ideator's formula; S=400 b/s, C=0.5 s, D=1.0 s; r=0.9825; max 13.87x by composition and 4.93x by yield; about 36% (24.6-48.5%) of on-target molecules ejected in error. Opened PMC10344778 (BOSS-RUNS): 87.5% fewer low-coverage sites at 1% abundance, 3.9-4.0x yield for 0.1% species, run on a real GridION. Opened PMC11065473: SimReadUntil is a CPU real-time-replay simulator with acceleration but no reported speed factor. Opened PMC11610257: 458 positive blood cultures, adaptive-sampling host depletion, species in 1 h, AMR needed 15 h. Opened the UEA record for Charalampous 2019. No RL or LLM-written ReadUntil policies were found by search (absence, not proof).
top.main_risk: The read classifier is a confusion-matrix abstraction, so any gain is only as good as the assumed error rates; sweep them. BOSS-RUNS already does principled dynamic policies, so the claim must be 'matches or beats BOSS-RUNS, found by agent plus GPU search'. Dynamic-policy gains are not validated on hardware this weekend; only static policies validate against Martin. The physical chip is operated, not designed, and the demo is less striking than a field or particle render.
top.headline_metric: Median simulated hours to a confident AMR-gene call (e.g. 20x coverage of the carried resistance genes) after species ID, agent policy vs static human depletion vs a BOSS-RUNS-style rule, after the simulator first reproduces Martin 2022's enrichment numbers. Second: simulated flow-cell-hours per wall-clock second on GPU vs SimReadUntil.

top.title: Zonation-by-design: agent-designed gas-channel layouts that set the in-vivo oxygen gradient in a liver chip (absorbs seed S3, gut-chip oxygen gradient)
top.description: Liver cells behave differently along the oxygen gradient from the portal vein to the central vein, and most liver chips are uniformly oxygenated. In the ZoC chip, two serpentine gas channels (air and nitrogen) in a PDMS layer under the cell chamber set three oxygen zones by diffusion through the PDMS. An agent writes channel-routing code under fabrication rules. A batched 3-D voxel diffusion solver with Michaelis-Menten cell uptake scores each layout against a target oxygen map (a linear in-vivo profile, three zones, or an assay-specific map). The same engine could serve a gut-chip oxygen target (seed S3), but that is a weaker stand-alone problem. The comparison baseline is the ZoC hand layout simulated in the same solver.
top.scores: hardware 4, AI loop 4, biotech/money 4, visual 4, parallelism 3, feasibility 4, honesty 5 = 28/35
top.verified: Opened PMC11828804 (ZoC): two serpentine gas channels 0.2 x 0.1 mm, air 19% and N2 0%; O2 diffusivity 2.69e-9 (medium) and 3.25e-9 m2/s (PDMS); measured zones without cells about 19%, 12-14% and 6-8%, with HepG2 about 19%, 10-11% and 3-5.5%; COMSOL 6.0. Michaelis-Menten Km = 6.3e-3 mol/m3 and per-cell uptake q = 3.5e-16 mol/s are given in the paper, so these are no longer unverified. Prior art: 'Generation of oxygen gradients with arbitrary shapes in a microfluidic device' (Lab Chip, doi 10.1039/b920401f, found by search, not opened) makes arbitrary gradients by switching gas mixtures. No inverse design toward a target oxygen map was found. Emulate DILI value claim not re-opened in this round.
top.main_risk: A compute-minded judge may see the GPU as optional, since one steady diffusion solve is seconds on a CPU, and may ask why not plain adjoint or topology optimisation, which suits a smooth diffusion problem better than an agent. The demo shows oxygen only; it cannot show that cells actually zonate or change toxicity readouts.
top.headline_metric: RMS error (mmHg) between the achieved and target periportal-to-pericentral profile, agent layout vs the ZoC layout in the same solver, at equal or fewer gas lines, after reproducing ZoC's measured zone values. Plus layouts per minute on GPU vs CPU.

top.title: Field Sculptor: agent-designed electrode layouts for impedance blood counting without focusing
top.description: A coplanar impedance cytometer counts and sizes cells as they pass over electrodes on a chip floor, but the signal depends on how high each cell flows, so identical cells read as different sizes unless extra hardware focuses them. An agent writes electrode-layout generators (number, widths, gaps, floating or grounded bypass electrodes, wiring), inventing new topologies, not only tuning numbers. A batched 3-D Laplace solve in a rectangular channel plus a reciprocity shortcut turns each layout into the signals for thousands of random cell paths, and the score is sizing CV. Correction: for the coplanar chip, Caselli's velocity correlation is 0.66 conventional vs 0.96 novel; the 0.90 vs 0.99 pair is the facing-electrode chip.
top.scores: hardware 5, AI loop 5, biotech/money 3, visual 3, parallelism 4, feasibility 4, honesty 4 = 28/35
top.verified: Opened PMC6190262 (Caselli 2017): corrected-diameter CVs of 3.3/1.6/1.4% (facing) and 4.3/2.4/1.8% (coplanar) for 5/6/7 um beads; coplanar channel 40 x 21.5 um; about 150,000 FE degrees of freedom. Opened PMC11048680 (Wu 2024): 5 um bead amplitude CV of 19.07% (no bypass), 9.63% (floating) and 9.21% (grounded); SNR 17.64, 21.62 and 29.37 dB; COMSOL used. Search found only manual or COMSOL layout comparisons and ML used for signal post-processing (de Bruijn, TU Delft record), with no automated layout search found.
top.main_risk: Absolute CVs will not match experiment, since electronics noise and velocity spread are not modelled, so only rankings can be claimed. The reciprocity shortcut breaks down near the electrodes. The money story (point-of-care blood counts) is diffuse, and the visual is weaker than particle streams.
top.headline_metric: Simulated 6 um bead sizing CV under unfocused random paths, agent layout vs standard two-pair, Caselli diagonal and Wu grounded-bypass layouts, after reproducing Wu's measured ranking (19.07% > 9.63% > 9.21%).

top.title: Drift-Proof Pulse: agent-designed square-wave readout and estimator for a continuous vancomycin aptamer sensor
top.description: Electrochemical aptamer sensors on a gold electrode can track drug levels in blood every few seconds, but their signal drifts as the surface layer degrades and fouls. The standard fix is a hand-picked two-frequency correction. An agent writes the readout programme (frequency set, amplitudes) and the estimator code, which are scored on about 10^5 simulated sensors with swept drift scenarios over a 24-hour dosing curve.
top.scores: hardware 4, AI loop 4, biotech/money 4, visual 3, parallelism 2, feasibility 5, honesty 3 = 25/35
top.verified: Opened PMC5660319 (Dauphin-Ducharme 2017): surface-confined Butler-Volmer square-wave model with k0 = 1.5 +/- 0.5 cm/s (monolayer) and 0.4 +/- 0.1 cm/s (DNA), alpha = 0.37, 20-1000 Hz, 25/50/75 mV, COMSOL. In-vivo and vancomycin papers were not opened this round.
top.main_risk: The drift model is the claim's weak point, because real fouling in blood is not first-principles, so the result is only robustness over an assumed scenario family. The GPU is close to optional: each voltammogram is a cheap closed-form update.
top.headline_metric: Fraction of 24 h measurements within +/-10% of true vancomycin concentration across the simulated sensor population, agent scheme vs two-frequency correction.

verdict.beats_front_runner: No, not clearly. The best new idea (DEP-Agent CTC chip) ties the front-runner on score (30/35 vs 30/35), and so does ReadUntil (30/35). DEP-Agent is stronger on: a real commercial device (ApoStream) with published numbers to validate against (crossover frequencies, 71-75% recovery, 99.33-99.85% PBMC depletion, the voltage trend); a clearer paying customer (pharma trial biomarker labs); a printable mask as the output; and a very visual particle-stream demo. It is weaker on: closer method prior art (COMSOL electrode sweeps and response-surface tuning already exist, so the novelty rests on agent-written multi-frequency topologies plus GPU population scoring); an empirical lift term that must be calibrated; and floor crowding, which likely limits real throughput but is not in the model. The heart-chip front-runner still has the more dramatic physics demo (spiral waves) and a stronger GPU-PDE story. Treat DEP-Agent as an equal alternative: pick it if the team prefers an oncology and liquid-biopsy pitch with hard validation numbers, otherwise keep the front-runner.
verdict.recommended: DEP-Agent (rank 1): agent-written electrode patterns and frequency schedules for a label-free CTC dielectrophoresis chip, validated against ApoStream. It is the strongest biochip-domain idea that meets all four constraints, and the only new one level with the front-runner. Headline metric: cells processed per hour (in 7.5 mL draw equivalents) at at least 70% predicted recovery across the NCI-60 solid-tumour lines and at least 99.33% PBMC depletion, against the simulated ApoStream operating point (1 draw per hour). Plus GPU vs CPU designs times cells per second.
verdict.plan_28h: H0-3 (engineer A): JAX Fourier-series potential above a periodic interdigitated array (Morgan 2001), checked against a small finite-difference solve. Add the single-shell Clausius-Mossotti factor using Gascoyne 2013 membrane capacitance and radius per cell type. Gate 1: reproduce the crossover frequencies, cancer lines 30-40 kHz and PBMCs 90-140 kHz at 30 mS/m. Source cytoplasm conductivity and mark it unverified until a URL is found. H0-3 (engineer B): agent harness with a design-function API (segments, gaps, frequencies, voltage, chamber height, flow schedule), a sandboxed executor, a per-line failure table and a CMA-ES baseline. H0-6 (medical student): CTC clinical story (EpCAM-negative tumours, trial biomarker reads), ApoStream's numbers and judge slides. H3-9: particle tracer with parabolic flow, sedimentation, DEP and an empirical lift term calibrated to 30 um levitation. Gate 2: reproduce the published operating point (71-75% recovery, 99.33-99.85% PBMC depletion) and the 2 to 4 Vpp trend. If absolute recovery misses, switch the claim to relative gains. H9-12: vmap over designs times about 10^5 cells; benchmark GPU vs a NumPy CPU loop for the parallelism number. H12-20: agent runs overnight: the LLM proposes topologies (e.g. a two-segment low then high frequency array aimed at monocytes), the GPU scores them, and a Pareto archive of recovery vs throughput fills in, alongside CMA-ES on the same budget. H20-25: demo with a live chip render (warm-coloured tumour cells and grey leukocytes streaming, peeling down or levitating), the code diff panel and the Pareto front filling in. Export the best electrode mask as a vector file. H25-28: lock numbers and rehearse. The pitch is one headline number against the ApoStream baseline, one GPU speed-up, and a clear list of what the model cannot claim (adhesion, crowding, clogging, viability).
killed: S2 perfusion network designer: Sexton et al., Science 2025 (Rapid model-guided design of organ-scale synthetic vasculature) already couples fast synthetic vascular-tree generation with hemodynamics, reports a more than 230-fold speed-up, and validates viability in printed tissue, so this would be a re-run.

S3 gut-on-chip oxygen gradient (stand-alone): the Ingber anaerobic intestine chip (Nat Biomed Eng 2019) gets its gradient from an anaerobic chamber plus cell consumption, leaving a thin design space. Its physics is folded into the liver-zonation idea (rank 3).

PK-on-a-network multi-organ chip: the ODE network is tiny, so the GPU is optional; the visual is weak; and Herland's parameter tables sit in an untranscribed supplement, which makes the reproduction itself a weekend risk.

ITP-Agent UTI chip: the Bercovici numbers check out, but stiff, sharp isotachophoresis fronts on a fixed JAX grid are a high build risk, and the 10x limit-of-detection gain is an extrapolation, not a simulated output.

Protocol Pilot (CiPA MEA): in-silico CiPA risk scoring is crowded, it overlaps the cardiac front-runner, porting Paci2020 to batched JAX and finding multi-channel IC50 data for all 28 drugs is a feasibility risk, and the published models disagree on drug responses.
